results.controlIntent: Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to: a. Perform configuration management during system, component, or service [Selection (one or more): design; development; implementation; operation; disposal]; b. Control the integrity of changes to [Assignment: organization-defined configuration items under configuration management]; manage the integrity of those changes; and document the integrity of those changes; c. Implement only organization-approved changes to the system, component, or service; d. Record approved changes to the system, component, or service; and record the potential security and privacy impacts of such changes; and e. Track security flaws and flaw resolution within the system, component, or service; and report findings to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel].

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two sources reveals a mixed conformance picture:

**Satisfied elements:**
- The initial endpoint deployment (CreateEndpoint at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z) occurred *after* the model registry approval (2025-12-01T09:00:00Z), satisfying the requirement that only organization-approved changes are implemented (SA-10.r4.c). The registry entry (id: 41205219) confirms formal approval status and records the approved version with lineage (ARN, version, timestamps), partially satisfying SA-10.r4.d.

**Not-satisfied elements:**
- The UpdateEndpoint event (2026-03-15T14:22:00Z, id: 80eecff8) deployed a hotfix config (`churn-predictor-v1-hotfix`) with **no corresponding model registry entry or approval record**. This directly violates SA-10.r4.c (implement only approved changes) and SA-10.r4.d (record approved changes and their security/privacy impacts). The change was made by the same IAM user without going through the registry approval workflow.
- There is no evidence of security flaw tracking or flaw-resolution reporting (SA-10.r4.e) in any retrieved evidence.
- The hotfix deployment lacks any documented security or privacy impact assessment (SA-10.r4.b/d).

**Temporal ordering is critical here:** the unapproved hotfix post-dates the compliant initial deployment by over three months, representing an ongoing gap in change-control discipline.
gaps: No model registry entry or approval record exists for the hotfix config 'churn-predictor-v1-hotfix' deployed 2026-03-15 — human attestation needed to determine if an out-of-band approval process was followed.
No evidence of security flaw tracking, flaw resolution records, or reporting to designated personnel (SA-10.r4.e) — a separate ticketing/ITSM system may hold this data but was not retrievable.
No security or privacy impact assessment documentation was found for either the initial deployment or the hotfix change (SA-10.r4.d partial requirement).

It is unclear whether 'data-scientist-jdoe' had authorization to deploy directly without registry approval — IAM policy evidence would clarify whether a preventive control should have blocked the hotfix.
